claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
The starting Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is an as-cast, single-phase solid solution.
The starting Co-free alloy has a fine, homogeneous microstructure.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a stable single-phase FCC solid solution with favorable mechanical properties over multiple temperatures.
Removing Co from CoCrFeMnNi increases the average stacking-fault energy.
Higher stacking-fault energy reduces the propensity for deformation twinning.
Co removal modifies dislocation-core structure and dislocation mobility in FeNiCrMn.
The dynamic response of Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed predominantly by temperature- and rate-dependent dislocation mobility rather than deformation twinning.
At low temperatures and high strain rates, hindered dislocation glide raises the yield strength of Co-free FeNiCrMn.
At low temperatures and high strain rates, the Co-free alloy exhibits reduced deformation twinning.
Reduced twinning decreases the capacity for twin-mediated accommodation of plastic strain.
At elevated temperatures and low strain rates, thermal activation promotes more homogeneous dislocation slip and restores ductility.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show a steeper increase in yield strength as temperature decreases.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show a steeper increase in yield strength as strain rate increases.
At equivalent test conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a lower deformation-twin fraction than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The two alloys will exhibit distinct strain-hardening responses under equivalent temperature and strain-rate conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies from approximately 300 K to 900 K and from approximately 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1, provided that secondary precipitation and significant grain growth do not occur.
A controlled comparison requires Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi samples with matched processing histories, grain sizes, phase constitution, temperatures, and strain rates.
The hypothesis is falsified if the Co-free alloy has no statistically significant reduction in twin activity and has temperature- and rate-dependent strength and ductility similar to the baseline.
